item.title: Latin Americans increasingly favor China in past two years, The Economist survey finds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
A student from Latin America poses with a Chinese student at an international cultural festival, Zhenjiang City, east China's Jiangsu Province, April 19, 2025. /VCG
Favorability toward China has continued to improve across Latin America over the past two years, according to a latest survey released by The Economist on September 30.
The latest Latinobarómetro poll, published by The Economist, shows that favorable views of China increased in 15 of the 17 Latin American countries surveyed: the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Costa Rica, Honduras, El Salvador, Ecuador, Peru, Guatemala, Colombia, Bolivia, Panama, Paraguay, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Argentina and Uruguay.
Among the 17 countries, Panama and Ecuador were the only two countries to see a slight decline in favorability toward China.
The survey also found that favorable views of the United States declined in 15 of the 17 countries surveyed over the same period.
"For the first time, in a historically pro-American region, more Latin Americans now see China’s influence as positive than that of the United States," The Economist said.
The magazine attributed the decline of US favorability in Latin America in part to US President Donald Trump's more confrontational approach toward a region he believes the United States should dominate.
The survey found that nearly two-thirds disapproved of Trump's handling of international relations.
The findings are broadly in line with a survey released by the Pew Research Center in July. It found that in 27 of the 36 countries and regions surveyed, people held more favorable views of China than of the United States.
Since 2023, the gap between favorable views of China and the US in those countries has steadily narrowed, before reversing in the 2026 survey. The median share of respondents with a favorable view of China stood at 46%, compared with 36% for the United States.

item.title: China's Shenzhou-23 astronauts send National Day greetings from space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Chinese astronauts Zhu Yangzhu (C), Zhang Zhiyuan (R) and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, for the upcoming Shenzhou-23 crewed spaceflight mission, meet the press at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, May 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Lian Zhen)
BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-23 astronauts aboard China's Tiangong space station sent video greetings to their motherland on Thursday, which is China's National Day and the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
Commander Zhu Yangzhu and his crewmates Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered their wishes for the country and its space program together as the station, about 400 km above Earth, flew over China.
"When we look at Earth from the space station, that brilliantly lit land is the motherland we miss day and night," said Li, the first astronaut from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to travel to space.
The three astronauts were launched aboard the Shenzhou-23 spaceship late on May 24 and have been in orbit for more than four months. They are in good condition, having completed in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-21 astronauts, repaired the station's solar panels in a spacewalk and deployed application payloads outside the station.
This year marks the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program. Remarkable milestones include the launch of the country's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System that offers global services, the Chang'e lunar missions, the Tianwen-1 Mars mission, the Tiangong space station and the steady advance of crewed lunar exploration project.
"We can never forget that in deserts, mountains and on islands, a group of people have gazed at the stars and kept striving, generation after generation, for 70 years, creating the glory of China's space program," said Zhang, who is on his first spaceflight.
Zhu, from China's third batch of astronauts, is on his second spaceflight after the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, and is commanding a long-duration mission for the first time. "The 'baton of history' has been passed to us. We will certainly run this leg well, and keep safeguarding and building our home in space," he said.

item.title: EU tightens migration chain as return rules approved
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
This photo taken on Jan. 29, 2025 shows the Berlaymont Building, the European Commission headquarters, in Brussels, Belgium. (Xinhua/Meng Dingbo)
Under the new Return Regulation, EU countries will operate under common return procedures, including a new European Return Order, and gain the option of establishing so-called "return hubs" in non-EU countries.
BRUSSELS, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The European Union (EU) member states on Thursday gave final approval to a new regulation to accelerate the return of people with no legal right to stay, adding an enforcement mechanism to migration and asylum rules that took effect in June.
According to the EU figure, around two in three people ordered to leave the bloc currently do not actually depart. The regulation complements the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, which took effect on June 12.
The pact sets common rules for screening, asylum procedures, responsibility among member states and solidarity mechanisms, while the new regulation focuses on returning people found to have no right to stay.
The European Commission earlier described returns as the "missing piece" of the pact, while European Parliament rapporteur Malik Azmani called return the "final piece in Europe's migration system."
PRESSURE FOR GREATER CONTROL
The tougher return rules came after a turbulent summer that again pushed migration high up Europe's agenda.
On July 30 and 31, tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, prompting Madrid to deploy the military and triggering calls from several European governments for tighter border controls.
People gather on the Moroccan side of the border with Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, preparing to cross into the enclave, on July 30, 2026. According to the Spanish government, at least 67 people died during the recent migrant crisis, while more than 48,000 of the nearly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta had returned to neighboring Morocco within 48 hours. (Photo by Liu Wenyong/Xinhua)
The crisis came only weeks after the migration pact entered into application and added urgency to a broader push for tougher enforcement.
Claire Kumar, head of policy and senior research fellow at ODI Europe, told Xinhua that public concern over irregular migration was strongly linked to a perceived "lack of control," with people expecting governments to demonstrate that borders and migration rules were effectively managed.
That pressure has become politically significant as mainstream parties face sustained pressure from right-wing and far-right forces advocating stricter migration controls, she added.
Pressure for further restrictions is also growing. Greece on Thursday proposed a mechanism that would allow EU countries to temporarily suspend asylum applications during large-scale arrivals deemed instrumentalized, with Germany, Austria, Denmark and Poland open to considering the idea.
These discussions suggest that the adoption of the Return Regulation may not mark the end of the EU's tightening migration agenda.
ENFORCEMENT MEETS REALITY
Yet passing a common return law does not guarantee a sharp rise in actual returns.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez (C) observes the work of the Civil Guard in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, on July 31, 2026. (La Moncloa/Handout via Xinhua)
The German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) said in a recent analysis that return hubs are likely to remain limited in scale and heavily dependent on cooperation with third countries.
It said that persistent obstacles include establishing migrants' identities, obtaining travel documents, securing cooperation from countries of origin, and finding third countries willing to host return facilities. Such problems cannot simply be bypassed by moving parts of the return process outside Europe.
At the same time, Europe's aging economies still need migrant workers, Kumar said.
She said that beneath increasingly restrictive political rhetoric, labor demand remains a powerful driver of migration. If adequate legal pathways are unavailable, workers may still fill those jobs through irregular or informal channels, increasing risks of exploitation and labor-market informality.
The next test is implementation: whether the EU can turn its new legal powers into more effective returns while its aging economies continue to need migrant labor.

item.title: Macao SAR celebrates National Day with flag-raising ceremony, reception
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
A flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China is held at the Golden Lotus Square in Macao, south China, October 1, 2026. /VCG
The government of China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on Thursday held a flag-raising ceremony and a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
The flag-raising ceremony took place at 8 a.m. at Macao's Golden Lotus Square. The national anthem was played, and China's national flag and the flag of the Macao SAR were hoisted.
The ceremony was followed by a reception hosted by the Macao SAR government at the China-Portuguese-speaking Countries Commercial and Trade Service Platform Complex.
Speaking at the event, Macao SAR Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai said the SAR government has proactively aligned with the country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), pooling wisdom and building consensus across all sectors to formulate and implement its own third five-year plan.
Looking ahead, the Macao SAR government will anchor its efforts on two key pillars – adopting refined governance with a "resident-centered" approach, as well as preventing and mitigating internal and external risks and challenges – thereby achieving sustainable development while effectively addressing these risks and challenges, Sam said.
He called for invigorating the market, enhancing the well-being of the people and striving to write a new chapter in the successful practice of "One Country, Two Systems" with Macao characteristics.

item.title: HKSAR gov't holds flag-raising ceremony, reception to celebrate National Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo)
HONG KONG, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) on Thursday held a flag-raising ceremony and a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
The flag-raising ceremony was held at the Golden Bauhinia Square on Thursday morning. The national anthem was played, and China's national flag and the flag of the HKSAR were hoisted.
The ceremony was followed by a reception hosted by the HKSAR government in the adjoining Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center.
Noting that this is the first National Day celebrated since the announcement of Hong Kong's first five-year plan, HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee said at the reception that the plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong to seize the opportunities brought by national development by applying its unique advantages under "one country, two systems."
"I am confident that as long as we, each dedicated to our respective roles, join hands and work in synergy with one another, Hong Kong will certainly be able to set out on a path to a brighter and more prosperous future," said Lee.
The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo)

item.title: China's September PMIs return to expansion amid firming recovery
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's manufacturing activity was back in expansion territory in September while non-manufacturing activity rebounded markedly, with both above the boom-bust line, official data showed on Wednesday, adding to signs of a firming recovery in the world's second-largest economy.
The purchasing managers' index (PMI) for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 in September 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from August and returning to the expansion zone, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signifies contraction.
The manufacturing sector's business climate improved further in September, with the PMI rising for a second consecutive month, said Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the NBS.
Among the 21 industries surveyed, 12 reported a PMI above the expansion threshold, four more than the previous month, Huo noted.
The sector saw expansion in both manufacturing output and market demand in September. The production sub-index climbed to 51.7, up 1.3 percentage points from August, while the new orders index was at 50.5, still above the threshold.
Driven by the acceleration in production, enterprises' willingness to purchase strengthened, with the procurement volume index reaching 51.0, an increase of 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, said Huo.
PMIs for the equipment manufacturing industry, the high-tech manufacturing industry and the consumer goods industry stood at 51, 52.5 and 50.7, respectively, all remaining in the expansion zone.
Affected by rising international commodity prices and growing demand in some industries, the purchasing price index for major raw materials and the ex-factory price index for manufacturing stood at 60.8 and 54, respectively, up 4.2 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points from the previous month.
PMIs for medium-sized and small manufacturing enterprises came in at 49.7 and 48.9, respectively, increases of 0.3 percentage points and 1 percentage point from the previous month, as business activity picked up.
Non-manufacturing activity also increased. The business activity index for the non-manufacturing sector reached 50.2 in September, a rise of 1.2 percentage points from August. The construction sector index rose 3.4 percentage points to 50.3, the highest level this year, while the services sector index increased by 0.9 percentage points to 50.2, with both returning to expansion.
"The traditional peak season and the upcoming National Day holiday have driven up demand in transportation, tourism and related consumer services," said Wu Wei, an analyst with the China Logistics Information Center.
The improvement came as a package of pro-growth measures was rolled out at a faster pace. The National Development and Reform Commission on Wednesday said it, together with the Ministry of Finance, had allocated the fourth and final batch of 62.5 billion yuan (around 9.28 billion U.S. dollars) in ultra-long special treasury bonds for consumer goods trade-in programs, bringing this year's total to 250 billion yuan.
Starting Oct. 1, China will implement interest subsidies for housing loans for eligible first-home buyers, offering an annualized subsidy of 1 percentage point on loans of up to 1 million yuan for up to five years, the Ministry of Finance and other departments said.
The People's Bank of China, China's central bank, announced a raft of strengthened support measures on Tuesday, including cutting the one-year interest rate of the pledged supplementary lending (PSL) facility from 1.75 percent to 1.5 percent, to better incentivize policy banks to support the real economy and serve national strategies.
It has also decided to increase the quota of the relending facility for sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades by 200 billion yuan and for agriculture and small and micro businesses by 500 billion yuan, out of which 300 billion yuan is dedicated to financial support for private firms.
"The recent policy mix is characterized by stepped-up counter-cyclical adjustments and the concentrated rollout of incremental tools," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank.
"With existing policies becoming more effective and incremental policies continuing to be introduced, economic momentum is expected to pick up further in the fourth quarter," he noted.
Looking ahead, China's manufacturing sector is expected to maintain steady and moderate expansion in the fourth quarter, said Wen Tao, an analyst with the China Logistics Information Center, citing accelerated implementation of major projects, including about 2 trillion yuan of planned investment by central state-owned enterprises in six major infrastructure networks this year.

item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
China's National Day falls on Oct. 1.
Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests.
"The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China."
He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability.
"We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said.
Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said.
Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said.
Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy.
He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added.
He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification.
China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said.
The Communist Party of China and state leaders Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attend a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China along with around 800 guests at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, presides over a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)

item.title: China outlines sci-tech priorities for 2026-2030 to underpin high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will strengthen basic research, tackle core technologies and speed up the industrial application of research results during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to better support high-quality development, officials of the Ministry of Science and Technology said on Tuesday.
At a press conference held by the State Council Information Office, Minister of Science and Technology Yin Hejun said China's total R&D spending exceeded 3.92 trillion yuan (about 582 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or 2.8 percent of GDP. This amount exceeded the average among the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) members for the first time.
China has ranked first in the world for many consecutive years in international patent applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and in papers published in high-level international journals, Yin said.
China ranks ninth among 60 countries in overall national innovation capability, according to the National Innovation Index Report 2025 released by the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology for Development.
Looking ahead, basic research will be organized in areas such as mathematical theory and applications, control of states of matter, synthetic biology, the materials genome, controlled nuclear fusion and intelligent scientist systems, Yin said.
He also called for faster application of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research to lead a shift in how research is carried out.
Paramount core technologies are another important priority, Yin said. China will push for progress along the entire innovation chain in key fields such as integrated circuits, machine tools and high-end instruments, and step up R&D in frontier technologies including AI, quantum technology, biotechnology and brain-computer interfaces.
Sci-tech innovation should also deliver more quality products and services that improve people's well-being, he said, with tasks laid out in areas including environmental pollution control, resource recycling, agricultural biological breeding, innovative drug development, high-end medical equipment and responses to population aging.
On turning research results into real-world productivity, Zhang Guangjun, vice minister of science and technology, said China will break the stereotype of producing results first and considering their application later on. Policies will instead direct research to where demand lies and ensure that results, once achieved, can be put to use, so that scientific and industrial innovation are planned in tandem and support one another, he said.
Zhang also called for stronger enterprise-led collaboration among industry, universities and research institutes, with innovation resources such as projects, platforms, data, talent and funding channeled to enterprises. Proof-of-concept and pilot-scale testing platforms will be built to help technologies mature and upgrade faster, he said.
Venture capital has played a vital role, with investors increasingly backing early-stage and small companies, taking a long-term view and focusing on hard technology, said Qiu Yong, vice minister of science and technology. New funds raised in the equity investment market exceeded 1 trillion yuan in the first half of 2026, up 49 percent year on year, he said, citing statistics from relevant institutions.
Universities are adjusting their disciplines to meet urgent national needs, he said.
China will continue to build Beijing and the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, Shanghai and the wider Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into international sci-tech innovation centers, Yin said. The three centers account for 58.8 percent of the country's R&D spending and 81.1 percent of its PCT international patent applications, and are helping drive innovation in surrounding provinces and municipalities and across the country.
R&D spending in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region has reached 4.48 percent of regional GDP, with major sci-tech achievements emerging in fields such as AI and biomanufacturing, Yin said.
The Yangtze River Delta accounts for nearly 30 percent of the country's basic research spending, with corporate spending on basic research up 38.3 percent year on year in 2025. It has witnessed key breakthroughs in areas such as integrated circuits and quantum technology, he said.
The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area draws on Guangdong's industrial innovation strengths and the science and education resources of Hong Kong and Macao, Yin said. Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao have jointly built 35 laboratories, and produced 14,000 papers under international collaboration.
